# Geometric Priors and Depth Integration

Also called: Geometric Regularization, Depth-Aware NeRF, Surface Priors

## Overview
This family of methods enhances standard Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) by integrating explicit geometric constraints—such as depth maps, signed distance fields (SDF), or Structure-from-Motion (SfM) features—into the optimization process. While standard NeRF [Link to NeRF] relies solely on photometric consistency to infer geometry, these methods solve the ambiguity inherent in sparse-view or ill-posed reconstruction problems by enforcing metric or structural geometric priors. They differ from siblings like [AdaNeRF](6195-adanerf.md) (which adapts sampling) or [SinNeRF](6199-sinnerf.md) (which uses sinusoidal activations) by explicitly conditioning the radiance field on external geometric signals to ensure topological correctness and metric accuracy.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family build on the canonical NeRF architecture defined in [Specific Model Architectures](8585-specific-model-architectures.md), which maps 6D coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ to density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ using coupled MLPs with positional encoding [Parent].

The core modification lies in the **loss function** and **sampling strategy**:
1.  **Geometric Loss Terms:** Unlike standard NeRF which minimizes only photometric error ($L_{rgb}$), these methods add regularization terms derived from geometric priors. Common terms include:
    *   **Depth Consistency:** Penalizing the difference between rendered depth and estimated/prior depth (e.g., $L_{depth}$ in [SfMNeRF](8664-sfmnerf.md), $L_{DOF}$ in [DASNeRF](8668-dasnerf.md)).
    *   **Surface Constraints:** Using SDFs to enforce zero-crossings at surfaces (e.g., [Neural RGB-D Surface Reconstruction](11352-neural-rgb-d-surface-reconstruction.md)).
    *   **Epipolar/Feature Constraints:** Enforcing multi-view consistency of 3D points derived from 2D feature matches (e.g., [SfMNeRF](8664-sfmnerf.md)).
2.  **Depth-Guided Sampling:** Many methods replace uniform or hierarchical sampling with depth-guided sampling. By estimating depth (via priors or auxiliary networks), samples are concentrated near surfaces, improving efficiency and detail [DASNeRF](8668-dasnerf.md), [DINER](11354-diner.md).
3.  **Hybrid Representations:** Some methods replace the density-based volume rendering with surface-based rendering (TSDF) or use cost volumes to extract geometric features before feeding them to the MLP [GeoNeRF](8710-geonerf.md), [Neural RGB-D Surface Reconstruction](11352-neural-rgb-d-surface-reconstruction.md).

## Subtopics

### [SfMNeRF](8664-sfmnerf.md)
Integrates Structure-from-Motion (SfM) constraints (matched SIFT features, epipolar geometry) into the NeRF training loop. It uses a pyramidal optimization strategy and explicit 3D position constraints for matched features to reduce geometric ambiguity in sparse views. Choose this when precise multi-view geometric consistency is required without dense depth sensors.

### [DASNeRF](8668-dasnerf.md)
Uses monocular depth priors from DepthAnythingV2 and a dynamic sampling mechanism. It enforces Depth Ordering Fidelity and Structural Consistency. Choose this for sparse-view reconstruction where deep learning-based depth estimation provides strong initial geometric cues.

### [GeoNeRF](8710-geonerf.md)
Replaces the standard MLP with a geometric morphology reasoner using 3D cost volumes and Transformers. It extracts view-independent and view-dependent tokens from cascading cost volumes. Choose this when generalizing to new scenes is prioritized over per-scene optimization, leveraging explicit multi-view stereo cues.

### [Neural RGB-D Surface Reconstruction](11352-neural-rgb-d-surface-reconstruction.md)
Uses a Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) instead of density for geometry, combined with a radiance field for appearance. It optimizes camera poses and latent codes. Choose this when high-quality, watertight mesh extraction is required and RGB-D input is available.

### [DINER](11354-diner.md)
Conditions the NeRF on depth deviation from estimated depth maps for sparse, high-disparity views. It uses depth-guided sampling and per-view feature maps. Choose this for novel view synthesis from very few (e.g., 4) widely separated views where standard NeRF fails due to lack of correspondence.

### [Volume Rendering Prior (VRPrior)](14662-volume-rendering-prior-vrprior.md)
Replaces handcrafted UDF-to-density mappings with a learned neural network $f_w$ that considers spatial context of neighbors. It learns a robust mapping from unsigned distances to alpha-blending weights. Choose this for surface reconstruction from multi-view RGB-D data where accurate surface representation is critical.

## Background
The integration of geometric priors into NeRF emerged to address the "slab" artifacts and geometric inaccuracies of standard NeRF, particularly in sparse-view settings. Early work like [SfMNeRF](8664-sfmnerf.md) demonstrated that explicit multi-view constraints could stabilize training. Subsequent works like [DASNeRF](8668-dasnerf.md) and [DINER](11354-diner.md) leveraged advances in monocular depth estimation (e.g., DepthAnythingV2) to provide dense geometric priors without additional hardware. Methods like [Neural RGB-D Surface Reconstruction](11352-neural-rgb-d-surface-reconstruction.md) shifted the representation from density to SDF to enable direct mesh extraction. [GeoNeRF](8710-geonerf.md) and [VRPrior](14662-volume-rendering-prior-vrprior.md) further explored explicit geometric structures (cost volumes, neighbor-based density prediction) to improve generalization and surface fidelity.
